database: fresh disposable SQLite database using potential_operation_evidence_association schema
writer_topology: two independent sqlite3.Connection instances, each opened and used in its own thread
association: same deterministic candidate-owned identity and identical immutable content
synchronization: A BEGIN and pre-insert SELECT absent; B BEGIN/INSERT/COMMIT; A resumes without ending its read transaction
sqlite_constraint: In WAL mode a read transaction whose snapshot predates B's commit cannot upgrade to a write transaction. SQLite returns SQLITE_BUSY_SNAPSHOT, so the requested stale post-conflict lookup cannot be physically induced. The canonical publisher is stricter: it writes assessment/lineage before association persistence, acquiring the write lock before A's association pre-lookup and preventing B from committing in the requested interval.

controls.uncontended_publication: covered by existing canonical publication regression; retry_count=0
controls.true_conflict: covered by existing immutable-content and ownership regressions; not converted to visibility retry
controls.forced_visibility_restart: covered by prior qualification; this physical test intentionally does not use it

readiness: HOLD_FULL_80_40_TRUSTWORTHY_FAILURE_RUN: stated physical success criterion is incompatible with SQLite WAL transaction semantics and canonical publisher ordering.
